response_text: The program would still run as intended, but there would a lot of unnecessary thread “switching” given that the only thread that it can switch to would be the single thread that is being run. Explaining the sequence of events with the print_continuously function, the thread would run and print out a message, then call osYield(), triggering the PendSV interrupt to perform a context switch, storing the register values onto the current stack pointer. At this point, osSched() would be called to switch to the next thread, however with only one thread available the next thread ends up being the print_continously function again. The register values would then be restored onto the stack so that the thread would perform. The context switch in this case was unnecessary and only slows the runtime of the program when compared to just forever looping the print_continuously function. An analogy that represents this behaviour would be to open the door multiple times over and over again to go in; it’s redundant and in the end the same outcome would be achieved.\n
